title: Plan-class admission broker with usage smoothing and model-variant spillover
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: Free-tier burst traffic and a small number of noisy tenants are causing tail-latency regressions for paid customers during regional capacity pressure. We need a plan-aware admission component that enforces fairness and predictable cost while minimizing cold starts and preserving latency SLOs.

Proposal summary: Implement a Plan-class Admission Broker (PAB) that: (1) maintains per-plan and per-tenant credit buckets with configurable decay and soft-borrow windows; (2) maps admitted requests into three runtime lanes — fast (prewarmed, low-quant), normal (default), deferred (batch or cached); (3) performs model-variant spillover when a lane is overloaded (e.g., redirect paid requests to quantized variant rather than full-precision fallback); (4) applies region-aware weights so global plan credits can be partitioned by region to avoid cross-region starvation; (5) emits rich telemetry for per-plan P99/P95 and token-cost.

Why different from existing admission controllers: instead of strictly hard quotas or single global token-buckets, PAB uses smoothing and controlled borrowing with a short-term debt reconciliation window to allow burst forgiveness without undermining paid SLAs. Model-variant spillover reduces failure modes where requests are dropped or sent to a much slower fallback model.
acceptance_criteria: PAB can route requests into fast/normal/deferred lanes based on plan and current credits
Per-plan credit buckets exposed in metrics and dashboard (consumption, balance, debt)
When fast lane is saturated, paid-plan requests either borrow (within policy) or spillover to quantized model variant with <5% quality regression (measured by eval set)
Latency SLOs (P95 and P99) for paid plans do not regress by more than 10% vs baseline under 2x burst compared to current routing
Automated simulation tests (loadgen) demonstrate borrower recovery within configured reconciliation window and no cross-region credit bleed
activity: 2025-11-10 - Ava created ticket and drafted PRD + initial design sketch (confluence: https://confluence.redwoodinfra/plan-class-admission-broker)
2025-11-14 - Spike complete: simulated mixed workload showing free-tier bursts increase paid P99 by 45% without smoothing. Spike notebook: https://gist.github.com/redwood/spike-plan-class-2025
2025-11-18 - Design review with runtime and infra teams. Decision: use leaky-bucket with exponential decay parameter per plan, borrow window default 30s, max debt factor 1.5x monthly allocation.

2025-11-20 - RFC posted for feedback (internal RFC: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rfcs/pull/128). Main feedback: add per-tenant override flag for enterprise SLA and a circuit-breaker for sustained debt.
2025-11-22 - Implementation branch opened: github: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/7645 (PAB admission broker core + metrics hooks)

2025-11-25 - Perf tests on staging: fast-lane prewarm reduced tail latency by 28% for paid plan under 2x burst, but observed increased cost by ~6% due to warm pools. Added autoscaling policy to mitigate cost.

2025-11-27 - Code review notes from Sofia Chen: tighten concurrency window for credit updates to avoid race under heavy burst; add unit tests for borrow accounting. Assigned follow-ups to Ravi and Jun.
Next steps: complete concurrency fixes, add model-variant spillover integration with routing policy engine, and rollout canary to a single region with telemetry gating.
